learning_outcomes.text: Have a systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects for modeling structural elements using the finite element method.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve structural mechanics problems using the finite element method.
Be able to choose and apply the finite element method to structural mechanics problems.
Understand the finite element calculation method to analyze mechanical components and structures.
Be able to combine the theory and practice of the finite element method to solve structural mechanics problems.
Understand the different applicable finite element methods and techniques and their limitations in the analysis of structural mechanics problems.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Adequate knowledge of their branch of engineering including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Awareness of all implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and engineering practice standards.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component, or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental concepts. Rayleigh-Ritz method. Finite Element Method
Application of the method to the calculation of prismatic part structures: BAR and BEAM finite elements.
Application of the method to the calculation of two-dimensional solids: TRIANGLE and QUADRILATERAL elements.
Preprocessing and modeling techniques: element selection, meshing, use of symmetries, boundary conditions.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (practical group works, lab practices)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 40% from the final exam and 60% from continuous assessment. Continuous assessment is based on practical group works with developed codes. Attendance and completion of scheduled lab practices are mandatory to pass the course.
